finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the result, so any caller can overwrite any document's body.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled doc_id in the PUT /doc/<doc_id> path (docs.py:17) plus request body field body (docs.py:20). Precondition: caller reaches the route with g.user set, i.e. any authenticated user. g.user is set outside this directory.
finding.sink: docs.py:20 doc["body"] = request.json["body"], an unconditional write to a protected document.

trace.note: route PUT /doc/<doc_id> binds doc_id from the URL
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads any document by id with no owner scope
can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated; boolean return dropped
can_edit returns owner == user or user in editors; no side effects, does not stop the handler

finding.guards_checked: can_edit logic (docs.py:7-8) is correct but unused at line 19; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) would abort(403) but update_doc does not call it; no abort/return/raise between lines 18 and 20; update_title (docs.py:24-29) calls require_edit correctly so it is not affected; no decorator, before_request hook, or ownership check in this file (any such control would live outside this directory and is unverified).

verdict.guard_found: none effective. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is called as a bare statement at docs.py:19 and its bool is discarded. require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which would abort(403), is not called in update_doc. No abort, return, or raise sits between lines 18 and 20. No decorator or before_request hook exists in docs.py. update_title (docs.py:27) does call require_edit, so the flaw is specific to update_doc.
verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 evaluates can_edit(g.user, doc) and discards the result, so the unconditional write at docs.py:20 runs for any caller who reaches the route, while update_title at docs.py:27 correctly enforces require_edit. The attacker is any authenticated user, since g.user must be set for line 19 to run; the only unverified piece is whether a hook outside this directory enforces ownership, and nothing in the provided code does.
